Tulip Mania was an infamous economic phenomenon that took place in Holland in the 1630s. As the colorful flowers' popularity and value as status symbols grew, so did their price. Eventually, the most expensive tulips were selling for the price of mansions even before they were planted. By 1637, prices finally peaked, and this financial bubble experienced a legendary downturn. The government had to intervene and restore financial stability to those who had become bankrupt, but many investors were left financially ruined.

Text 2

Financial bubbles are an economic event where the price of an item skyrockets past its real value and then collapses when investors begin to realize that they will not be able to sell the product. In short, the existence of a financial bubble hinges on the participation of investors who fuel the frenzy. One notable example is the Tulip Mania bubble, in which investors had bet on the future demand for tulips, often trading contracts for bulbs that didn't yet exist. All investors should beware any investment opportunity that seems too good to be true;
